summary: Adds a "custom" tool driven by gitTool.toolPath/customArgs/customName and makes gitTool.toolPath accept a bare command resolved from PATH. Verified out of VS Code with a stubbed host: bare name, bare name plus args, ${repoPath} placeholder, full path in both slash styles, missing executable, empty toolPath, and a non-shim executable. tsc compiles clean; README updated; markdown checker reports no errors.

improvements.text: The custom tool label falls back to the executable basename, so a bare "commits" shows as lowercase "commits" in the status bar.
improvements.recommendation: Left as is: gitTool.customName overrides it and is documented; capitalising a user command would misname tools whose casing is meaningful.

improvements.text: Shell invocation for .cmd/.bat shims quotes each token with double quotes, which would break an argument that itself contains a double quote.
improvements.recommendation: Accepted risk: git tool arguments are paths and flags; revisit only if a real tool needs embedded quotes.

positives.text: PATH resolution was generalised in resolveUserExe rather than special-cased for the custom tool, so every built-in also accepts a bare name in gitTool.toolPath.

verdict.rationale: No critical or high findings; the two improvements are recorded as accepted tradeoffs.
